judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the teaser thumbnail for the 'Off-duty officer...' story; the crop and the article page's caption ('GMP HQ, Newton Heath (stock image)') show it is a stock photo of the Greater Manchester Police HQ building. claimTrue: the alt is the headline, describing an officer attacking cops, which the photo does not show. The pattern is a news teaser thumbnail whose alt repeats the headline that sits right after it in a separate heading link (the img is not inside the link). Duplicating the headline is a redundancy that axe and most audit practice treat as best practice; whether a thumbnail alt that names the story instead of describing the photo fails 1.1.1 is a point on which competent auditors split (some fail it as not describing the image, or as a non-null alt on an image that should be decorative, F39; others pass it because the alt identifies the story the image illustrates). My lean is that this illustrative stock image does not fail (the alt identifies the story; it would ideally be alt=""), but the disagreement is real, so the label is uncertain. captureDiffers: the live page still has this card with the same img, alt and structure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header's sign-in button, an icon-only control (aria-label 'User Avatar - redirects to sign in and sign up'). The live markup and CSS confirm the icon is drawn with stroke var(--color-com-header-primary-nav-avatar-bg) = #ffffff on a transparent button over the primary header background #f0ba00 (xl-v2.css tokens, used at the 1280px viewport); the only other path is white at 16% opacity. White on #f0ba00 is about 1.79:1, below the 3:1 that 1.4.11 requires for the visual information needed to identify a component, and the icon is all the control shows. The claim states this accurately. captureDiffers: the live HTML and token stylesheet match the capture (the full-page screenshot leaves the header area blank, but the measured colours agree with the CSS).

judgments.label: true_positive

Read in good faith, as the rubric's example of an alternative that leaves out most of what the image conveys, the claim points at this alt as not matching the image, so it is a true positive. captureDiffers: the consent dialog (with the UK 'Reject and Pay' option) is what a first-time UK visitor receives; the live CMP config still sets the same cmp-MEN-logo image. I could not render the dialog myself, but nothing suggests a different version.

judgments.rationale: The element is the teaser thumbnail for 'Why Mauricio Pochettino held three-hour meetings with Manchester United players'. The crop shows a man in a black jacket with his arm round players in Manchester United training kit, and the linked article's figure (same Getty image, alt 'Mauricio Pochettino') is captioned 'Mauricio Pochettino spent three hours holding meetings with Manchester United players on Thursday'. claimTrue: the alt names what the image shows (Pochettino with United players at those meetings), so the claim is false. elementFails: the alt identifies the people and occasion pictured; it duplicates the headline (a best-practice redundancy), but it does not fail 1.1.1. The checker had the crop and judged wrongly: model_error. captureDiffers: the live page has the same image with a shortened alt ('Why Pochettino held three-hour meetings with United players'); no difference touches the claim.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Court' link in the mobile navigation curtain, inside the nested list 'News Submenu' under the list item 'News' (link 'News' plus 'Show submenu for News'); it goes to the Manchester Crown Court topic page. By this round's rule the parent list item of a nested list counts as context (H81), so the purpose, court news within News, is determinable from the link text with its context, and the destination matches it; 'Court' is also a normal section label on a news site. claimTrue: 'nothing around it does' is false, since the nested-list context is in the snapshot (the ancestors show it). elementFails: no. The curtain is sr-only and inert at this width (the AX tree marks it ignored, inertElement), so users meet it only when the menu opens, with the same context. The checker had the ancestors and judged wrongly: model_error. captureDiffers: the live HTML has the same inert curtain and the same link.
